title: Vaani Telugu — Spoken-First A0 to C2

baseLanguage.name: English
baseLanguage.designRule: All meanings/glosses are keyed by base-language code so another base language can be added later without changing Telugu concept IDs.

contentStatus.note: This file is designed as the stable master course contract and contains a high-confidence spoken-first seed corpus. No finite static file can itself guarantee C2; C2 requires extensive unseen listening/interaction and native-reviewed advanced corpus. The schema is intended not to require restructuring when more reviewed Telugu corpus/audio is added.

displayPolicy.script: Always store and display Telugu script.
displayPolicy.romanization: Always available on demand; shown by default for beginner material.
displayPolicy.meaning: Every first exposure must display an English meaning. Every learner-facing Telugu token/chunk must support hover/tap gloss resolution.
displayPolicy.audio: Every production-target item should support audio; human/native-reviewed audio is preferred, TTS may be fallback.
displayPolicy.unknownWordRule: A0-A2: never require a learner to understand/produce an unexplained lexical concept. B1-C2 inference tasks may contain unfamiliar language only when explicitly marked and hover/tap glosses remain available.

sessionPolicy.rule: There is no fixed daily ceiling. Each session independently receives an adaptive new-content allowance. A learner studying 3-4 hours may receive new content in later sessions if retention/review burden remains healthy.

guidance.condition: strong retention and >=90% independent recall with manageable review backlog

adaptiveNewContent.important: These are planner bands, not a proficiency score and not a daily cap.

newConceptIntroductionContract: show at least one natural context
never grade a word before its first explained exposure

sessionMix.principle: Interleave new material, same-session recall, due reviews, listening and speaking rather than blocking all new words together.
sessionMix.advancedRule: As level and review burden rise, reduce new-word proportion and increase extended listening, spontaneous speaking and transfer.

rules: Failed recall schedules earlier review and/or re-teaching in a different context.
Correct-after-hint is weaker evidence than independent recall.
Very slow correct recall is weaker evidence than fluent recall.
Fast independent delayed recall expands spacing.
Repeated contextual success is required before strong mastery.
Speaking and listening evidence are tracked separately from simple recognition.

contentRules: Prefer natural contemporary spoken Telugu over bookish/formal wording for production targets.
Keep useful formal/written alternatives as register variants rather than deleting them.
Use stable concept IDs independent of spelling.
Do not create a new concept merely because spelling/romanization was corrected.
A concept may have multiple natural accepted responses.
Do not force literal English-to-Telugu word order.
Do not use one exact canned sentence as the only valid conversational response.
Modern natural loanwords may be taught when they are genuinely common in speech.
Regional variants must be labeled; broad contemporary Telugu is the default productive target.

units.title: Sound before script
units.goal: Understand and reproduce the core sound contrasts used in common speech.

units.title: First contact
units.goal: Greet, give a name, ask a name, say yes/no, thank and apologise.

units.title: Immediate needs
units.goal: Ask for water, food, help and a bathroom.

units.title: Here and there
units.goal: Understand basic location and movement.

units.title: People around me
units.goal: Identify close family and common people.

units.title: Numbers and time basics
units.goal: Use 1-10, simple prices and now/today/tomorrow.

units.title: Daily routine
units.goal: Talk about waking, eating, going, working and sleeping.

units.title: Food and ordering
units.goal: Order common food/drink and change a simple order.

units.title: Shopping
units.goal: Ask price, quantity, choose and pay.

units.title: Travel
units.goal: Use bus/train/auto, ticket, destination and simple directions.

units.title: Home and family
units.goal: Describe home, family and possession.

units.title: Health basics
units.goal: Say pain, fever, medicine and need a doctor.

units.title: Work and study
units.goal: Say where you work/study and basic tasks.

units.title: Social basics
units.goal: Likes, invitations, simple feelings and plans.

units.title: Past events
units.goal: Explain what happened yesterday or earlier.

units.title: Plans and future
units.goal: Talk about tomorrow, weekend and future intentions.

units.title: Descriptions
units.goal: Describe people, places, objects and differences.

units.title: Requests and services
units.goal: Handle repairs, deliveries, appointments and service problems.

units.title: Longer social talk
units.goal: Sustain several turns about interests, family and experiences.

units.title: Phone and messaging
units.goal: Handle simple calls, missed calls and messages.

units.title: Reasons and choices
units.goal: Give simple reasons and preferences.

units.title: Unexpected problems
units.goal: Lost item, wrong route, delay and misunderstanding.

units.title: Connected storytelling
units.goal: Tell a coherent personal story with sequence, cause and result.

units.title: Opinions with reasons
units.goal: Explain and support an opinion on familiar topics.

units.title: Workplace conversation
units.goal: Participate in meetings, task updates and routine professional interaction.

units.title: Travel complications
units.goal: Handle cancellations, changes, complaints and alternatives.

units.title: Relationships and emotions
units.goal: Talk naturally about emotions, friendship and interpersonal problems.

units.title: Media and entertainment
units.goal: Discuss films, music, news and recommendations.

units.title: Explain how things work
units.goal: Give instructions and explain processes.

units.title: Unprepared conversation
units.goal: Maintain conversation when topic shifts unexpectedly.

units.title: Abstract discussion
units.goal: Discuss education, technology, environment and social change.

units.title: Debate without scripts
units.goal: State, defend, soften and revise a position.

units.title: Professional depth
units.goal: Present a problem, options, trade-offs and recommendation.

units.title: Native-speed everyday speech
units.goal: Follow fast connected conversational Telugu with normal repair.

units.title: Humour and implication intro
units.goal: Recognise common teasing, indirectness and implied stance.

units.title: Formal vs casual
units.goal: Switch appropriately between casual, polite and professional forms.

units.title: Long-form narrative
units.goal: Understand and produce extended stories and explanations.

units.title: Unfamiliar scenarios
units.goal: Transfer known language to situations not directly rehearsed.

units.title: Nuanced argument
units.goal: Express fine distinctions, reservations and layered reasoning.

units.title: Professional and academic speech
units.goal: Follow and contribute to specialised discussion in familiar domains.

units.title: Idiomatic conversation
units.goal: Understand and appropriately use common idiomatic/colloquial expressions.

units.title: Complex listening
units.goal: Follow long unscripted speech, interviews and discussions.

units.title: Mediation
units.goal: Explain, summarise and reformulate complex information for another person.

units.title: Style and register control
units.goal: Shift language according to relationship, purpose and setting.

units.title: Unrestricted spontaneous interaction
units.goal: Sustain precise, fluent speech across unfamiliar and demanding topics.

units.title: Fine shades of meaning
units.goal: Reformulate to express subtle distinctions and avoid ambiguity.

units.title: Implicit meaning and allusion
units.goal: Infer unstated links, humour, irony and culturally grounded allusion from context.

units.title: Complex synthesis
units.goal: Integrate and orally summarise multiple long sources and viewpoints.

units.title: Regional and colloquial comprehension
units.goal: Adapt to substantial variation in natural speech after reasonable acclimatisation.

units.title: C2 unseen performance
units.goal: Demonstrate ability on material and situations never rehearsed in the course.

assessmentPolicy.principle: Course completion does not equal proficiency.

levels.A0-A2: Primarily guided but must include delayed recall and unseen recombination.
levels.B1-B2: Increasingly unseen listening, multi-turn speaking, narration, explanation and transfer.
levels.C1-C2: Predominantly unseen extended material, spontaneous production, register/pragmatics, inference, synthesis and reformulation.

c2ExitCapabilities: follow long natural-speed speech with minimal support
express fine distinctions and reformulate precisely
understand common idiomatic and colloquial language in context
adapt register to relationship and setting
infer unstated links, humour and implication from context
sustain extended coherent speaking without scripted prompts

readingPolicy.rule: Telugu script is always present, but script decoding must not block early speaking progress. Romanization remains available. A dedicated literacy expansion may later deepen reading/writing without changing concept IDs.

mustPass: every lexical concept has stable id, Telugu, romanization and English meaning
every production item has an explained first exposure
every A0-A2 sentence/pattern has glossable component concepts
formal variants are not silently substituted for everyday spoken production forms
SRS includes 1,2,3,5,7,14 day milestones and continues indefinitely
contentValidation.nativeReviewGate: Before declaring the corpus linguistically final, a qualified native Telugu reviewer should approve pronunciation, spoken naturalness, register, regional neutrality and all C1/C2 idiomatic/pragmatic content.

grammarInUse.name: Reconciling views
grammarInUse.pattern: రెండు వాదనల్లోనూ కొంత నిజం ఉంది; తేడా ___లో ఉంది.
grammarInUse.romanization: rendu vaadanalonoo konta nijam undi; teda ___lo undi.

meaning.en: Both arguments contain some truth; the difference lies in ___.

grammarInUse.name: Source attribution
grammarInUse.usage: Attribute information without presenting it as your own direct observation.

exampleMeaning.en: According to the report, the results improved.

grammarInUse.name: Counterpoint
grammarInUse.usage: Acknowledge a point before giving a limitation or counterargument.
grammarInUse.exampleTelugu: అది నిజమే, కానీ ఖర్చు కూడా చూడాలి.

exampleMeaning.en: That is true, but we also need to consider cost.

grammarInUse.name: Probability
grammarInUse.usage: Express possibility/probability.

exampleMeaning.en: There is a chance it will be delayed.

grammarInUse.name: Reported viewpoint
grammarInUse.usage: Report a circulating or attributed view.

exampleMeaning.en: They are saying that change is needed.

grammarInUse.name: Contrastive comparison
grammarInUse.usage: Compare against a reference.

exampleMeaning.en: Compared with last year, cost decreased.

grammarInUse.name: Degree / extent
grammarInUse.usage: Express extent/limit.

exampleMeaning.en: I agree to some extent.

grammarInUse.name: Reformulation
grammarInUse.usage: Rephrase for clarity.

exampleMeaning.en: In other words, the problem is not money.

grammarInUse.name: Qualification
grammarInUse.usage: Limit or qualify a broad claim.
grammarInUse.exampleTelugu: కొంతవరకు నిజమే, కానీ అన్ని సందర్భాల్లో కాదు.

exampleMeaning.en: It is true to some extent, but not in every context.

grammarInUse.name: Perspective frame
grammarInUse.usage: Frame an issue from a particular perspective.

exampleMeaning.en: From the user perspective, this is easy.

grammarInUse.name: Caveat
grammarInUse.usage: Add an important limitation/caveat.
grammarInUse.exampleTelugu: అయితే, ఒక విషయం గుర్తుంచుకోవాలి: ఈ డేటా పరిమితమైనది.

exampleMeaning.en: However, one thing to remember is that this data is limited.

grammarInUse.name: Synthesis
grammarInUse.usage: Combine points into a conclusion.
grammarInUse.exampleTelugu: ఈ విషయాలను కలిపి చూస్తే మార్పు అవసరం.

exampleMeaning.en: Taken together, these points suggest change is needed.

grammarInUse.name: Non-absolute stance
grammarInUse.usage: Reject an overly absolute inference.

exampleMeaning.en: It is not necessarily bad.

grammarInUse.name: Dependence on context
grammarInUse.usage: Show context dependence.

exampleMeaning.en: The result depends on the situation.

grammarInUse.name: Scope restriction
grammarInUse.usage: Limit the scope of a generalisation.

exampleMeaning.en: This does not apply to every context.

grammarInUse.name: Precision reformulation
grammarInUse.usage: Replace an approximate statement with a more precise one.
grammarInUse.exampleTelugu: ఇంకా ఖచ్చితంగా చెప్పాలంటే, ప్రభావం అందరికీ ఒకేలా లేదు.

exampleMeaning.en: More precisely, the effect is not the same for everyone.

grammarInUse.name: Implicit inference
grammarInUse.usage: Describe an inferred meaning not explicitly stated.
grammarInUse.exampleTelugu: మాటల్లో చెప్పకపోయినా, అతనికి సందేహం ఉందన్న భావం ఉంది.

exampleMeaning.en: Though not said explicitly, there is a sense that he has doubts.

grammarInUse.name: Reconciling views
grammarInUse.pattern: రెండు వాదనల్లోనూ కొంత నిజం ఉంది; తేడా ___లో ఉంది.
grammarInUse.romanization: rendu vaadanalonoo konta nijam undi; teda ___lo undi.
grammarInUse.usage: Reconcile competing claims while retaining the actual difference.
grammarInUse.exampleTelugu: రెండు వాదనల్లోనూ కొంత నిజం ఉంది; తేడా ప్రాధాన్యంలో ఉంది.

exampleMeaning.en: Both arguments contain some truth; the difference is in priority.

grammarInUse.name: Alternative interpretation
grammarInUse.usage: Offer a plausible alternative interpretation.

exampleMeaning.en: This can also be interpreted as a refusal.

grammarInUse.name: Evidence-sensitive inference
grammarInUse.usage: State an inference conditional on available evidence.
grammarInUse.exampleTelugu: అందుబాటులో ఉన్న సమాచారాన్ని బట్టి, నిర్ణయం ఇంకా ఖరారు కాలేదు.

exampleMeaning.en: Based on the available information, the decision is not final yet.

grammarInUse.name: Metapragmatic contrast
grammarInUse.usage: Contrast literal meaning with contextual meaning.
grammarInUse.exampleTelugu: అక్షరార్థంగా అది అంగీకారం కాదు, కానీ సందర్భంలో సానుకూల సంకేతం కావచ్చు.

exampleMeaning.en: Literally it is not an agreement, but in context it may be a positive signal.

languageDirection.futureBaseLanguageRule: Add translations/glosses under meaning.<BCP47 language code>. Never change Telugu concept IDs when the base language changes.

productPriority.principle: Like first-language acquisition, early progress must not be blocked by literacy. Telugu script remains visible and learnable, but communication is the core progression signal.

finalDesignContract.importantTruth: No finite static corpus can guarantee C2 merely by completion. C2 is awarded only after repeated success on unseen, natural-speed, spontaneous tasks. This file contains the curriculum, content banks, generation contracts, quality gates and assessment rules needed to support that path.
finalDesignContract.nativeReviewGate: Before public release, Telugu production targets, audio, regional material, idioms and pragmatic C1/C2 material must be reviewed by qualified native Telugu linguists/speakers. This is a QA gate, not a schema/content-category gap.

c2ExitCriteriaDetailed.importantNote: These are Vaani descriptor-aligned product gates, not an official CEFR certificate. CEFR C2 is not defined by a fixed vocabulary count.
mustDemonstrateRepeatedlyOnUnseenMateria: Understand virtually all modern general-purpose spoken Telugu across ordinary native speeds, with time to acclimatise to an unfamiliar accent.
Read complex abstract, specialised and literary Telugu with high independence.
Summarise and synthesise multiple spoken and written sources while preserving argument structure and stance.
Speak spontaneously at length with natural flow, precision and smooth self-repair.
Distinguish and express fine shades of meaning; avoid ambiguity through reformulation.
Understand and appropriately use common idiomatic expressions, colloquialisms and register shifts.
Maintain grammatical control while concentrating on planning, interaction and another speaker’s reactions.
Write complex, clear, audience-appropriate Telugu and transform style/register when required.
Infer unstated links, implications, humour and common allusions from context.
Mediate complex information for another person, adapting detail and language to the audience.
failureConditions: Relying on romanization for advanced reading
Using grammatically possible but pragmatically inappropriate register
Large dependence on hints or translation in advanced tasks

itemLevel: Telugu form reviewed for spelling and meaning
Natural spoken form separated from formal/written form when they differ
Natural English meaning is contextual rather than mechanically literal
Part of speech or construction type provided where meaningful
At least one natural example for productive vocabulary
Accepted natural alternatives included for open production
Native-linguist signoff required for C1/C2 idioms, dialect, humour, literary and subtle pragmatic items
corpusLevel: No unexplained vocabulary in beginner instructional examples unless intentionally inferable and cued
Dependency graph prevents sentences from depending heavily on untaught words
Spoken corpus is not dominated by bookish vocabulary
Formal Telugu is preserved and labelled rather than deleted
Regional forms are labelled rather than mixed into a false “neutral” standard
Advanced materials include authentic long-form input and not only isolated sentences
Audio contains multiple real speakers/accents for advanced levels; TTS alone cannot satisfy C2 listening coverage
Assessment uses unseen items and multiple skills

principles: Teach sound through high-frequency words before technical terminology.
Contrast vowel length where it changes or strongly affects intelligibility.
Train dental vs retroflex stops, geminates, aspiration where relevant, nasals, laterals/rhotics and connected speech.
Do not penalise harmless accent features if speech remains clear and natural.

codeSwitchingPolicy.principle: Contemporary spoken Telugu naturally uses many English loans/code-switches, especially in urban, technical and professional settings. Teach common natural forms when they are genuinely used; also teach Telugu/formal equivalents for recognition and register control.
codeSwitchingPolicy.doNotDo: Do not artificially replace every common loanword with a rare bookish equivalent in everyday speaking tasks.

turns.speaker: B

turns.speaker: B

turns.speaker: B

turns.speaker: B

turns.speaker: A
turns.telugu: సౌకర్యం కోసం కొంత డేటా ఇవ్వడం తప్పేనా?
turns.romanization: saukaryam kosam konta data ivvadam tappe naa?

turns.speaker: B
turns.telugu: తప్పనిసరిగా కాదు. ఎంత డేటా, ఎందుకు, ఎంతకాలం అన్నది చూడాలి.
turns.romanization: tappanisaarigaa kaadu. enta data, enduku, entakaalam annadi choodaali.

meaning.en: Not necessarily. We need to consider how much data, why, and for how long.

turns.speaker: B
turns.telugu: కొంతవరకు ఒప్పుకుంటాను, కానీ “అందరికీ” అనడం ఎక్కువగా ఉంటుంది.

turns.speaker: B
turns.telugu: అవసరాలు ఒకేలా ఉండవు. సందర్భాన్ని బట్టి ప్రభావం మారొచ్చు.

meaning.en: Needs are not all the same. The impact can vary by context.

turns.speaker: B
turns.romanization: repu meeru vastaaraa ani maryaadagaa adugutaanu.

meaning.en: I would politely ask, “Will you be coming tomorrow?”

turns.speaker: B
turns.telugu: తప్పనిసరిగా కాదు. మాటల కంటే సందర్భం, ధోరణి కూడా ముఖ్యం.
turns.romanization: tappanisaarigaa kaadu. maatala kante sandarbham, dhorani koodaa mukhyam.

meaning.en: Not necessarily. Context and tone matter too.

turns.speaker: B
turns.telugu: ఈ సందర్భంలో అది నిర్ణయాన్ని వాయిదా వేసినట్టు ఉండొచ్చు. కానీ మరో సందర్భంలో నిజంగానే “తర్వాత చూద్దాం” అనవచ్చు.
turns.romanization: ee sandarbhamlo adi nirnayaanni vaayidaa vesinattu undochchu. kaanee maro sandarbhamlo nijangaane tarvaata chooddaam anavachchu.

meaning.en: Here it may postpone the decision, but elsewhere it can literally mean to consider it later.

turns.speaker: A
turns.telugu: ఒకరు వేగం ముఖ్యం అంటున్నారు; ఇంకొకరు నాణ్యత ముఖ్యం అంటున్నారు.
turns.romanization: okaru vegam mukhyam antunnaaru; inkokaru naanyata mukhyam antunnaaru.

meaning.en: One person says speed matters; another says quality matters.

turns.speaker: B
turns.telugu: రెండూ విరుద్ధంగా కనిపిస్తున్నా, అసలు తేడా ప్రాధాన్యంలో ఉంది.

listeningScripts.title: Simple introduction
listeningScripts.transcriptTelugu: హలో. నా పేరు దీప. నేను హైదరాబాద్‌లో ఉంటాను.
listeningScripts.romanization: halo. naa peru Deepa. nenu Hyderabad-lo untaanu.

summary.en: Deepa introduces herself and says where she lives.

listeningScripts.title: Morning routine
listeningScripts.transcriptTelugu: నేను ఉదయం ఆరు గంటలకు లేస్తాను. నీళ్లు తాగి టిఫిన్ తింటాను. తర్వాత ఆఫీస్‌కి వెళ్తాను. సాయంత్రం ఇంటికి వస్తాను.
listeningScripts.romanization: nenu udayam aaru gantlaku lestaanu. neellu taagi tiffin tintaanu. tarvaata office-ki veltaanu. saayantram intiki vastaanu.

summary.en: A simple daily routine.

comprehensionQuestions.en: What time does the speaker get up?
Where does the speaker go after breakfast?

listeningScripts.title: Running late
listeningScripts.transcriptTelugu: ఈరోజు నేను ఆలస్యంగా బయల్దేరాను. రోడ్డుమీద ట్రాఫిక్ చాలా ఎక్కువగా ఉంది. బస్ కూడా ఆలస్యంగా వచ్చింది. అందుకే మీటింగ్‌కి ఆలస్యం అవుతోంది. నేను మేనేజర్‌కి మెసేజ్ పంపాను.
listeningScripts.romanization: ee roju nenu aalasyangaa bayalderaanu. road-meeda traffic chaalaa ekkuvagaa undi. bus koodaa aalasyangaa vachchindi. anduke meeting-ki aalasyam avutondi. nenu manager-ki message pampaanu.

summary.en: The speaker is late because of traffic and a delayed bus and informs the manager.

listeningScripts.title: Choosing where to live
listeningScripts.transcriptTelugu: ఆఫీస్‌కి దగ్గరగా ఉంటే ప్రయాణ సమయం తగ్గుతుంది. కానీ అక్కడ అద్దె ఎక్కువ. కొంచెం దూరంగా ఉంటే అద్దె తక్కువగా ఉంటుంది, కానీ రోజూ ట్రాఫిక్‌లో ఎక్కువ సమయం గడపాలి. డబ్బు ఆదా చేయడం కూడా ముఖ్యం, సమయం ఆదా చేయడం కూడా ముఖ్యం.
listeningScripts.romanization: office-ki daggaragaa unte prayana samayam taggutundi. kaanee akkada adde ekkuva. konchem doorangaa unte adde takkuvagaa untundi, kaanee roju traffic-lo ekkuva samayam gadapaali. dabbu aadaa cheyadam koodaa mukhyam, samayam aadaa cheyadam koodaa mukhyam.

summary.en: The speaker weighs commute time against rent.

comprehensionQuestions.en: What is the advantage of living near the office?

listeningScripts.title: Technology and privacy
listeningScripts.transcriptTelugu: టెక్నాలజీ వల్ల చాలా పనులు వేగంగా, సులువుగా అయ్యాయి. బ్యాంక్‌కి వెళ్లకుండా డబ్బు పంపగలం; కొన్ని పనులు ఇంటి నుంచే చేయగలం. అయితే మన డేటా ఎక్కడికి వెళ్తోంది, ఎవరు ఉపయోగిస్తున్నారు, ఎంతకాలం నిల్వ చేస్తున్నారు అన్న విషయాలు కూడా తెలుసుకోవాలి. సౌకర్యం కోసం గోప్యతను పూర్తిగా వదులుకోవాల్సిన అవసరం లేదు.
listeningScripts.romanization: technology valla chaalaa panulu vegangaa, suluvugaa ayyaayi. bank-ki vellakundaa dabbu pampagalam; konni panulu inti nunche cheyagalam. aithe mana data ekkadiki veltundi, evaru upayogistunnaaru, entakaalam nilva chestunnaaru anna vishayaalu koodaa telusukovaali. saukaryam kosam gopyatanu poorthigaa vadulukovaalsina avasaram ledu.

summary.en: Technology brings convenience, but privacy still matters.

listeningScripts.title: Remote work
listeningScripts.transcriptTelugu: ఇంటినుంచి పని చేయడం వల్ల ప్రయాణ సమయం తగ్గుతుంది, కొందరికి ఏకాగ్రత కూడా పెరగొచ్చు. అదే సమయంలో, టీమ్‌లో అనౌపచారికంగా జరిగే చిన్న సంభాషణలు తగ్గిపోతే సమాచారం పంచుకోవడం, కొత్తవాళ్లు టీమ్‌లో కలవడం కాస్త కష్టమవచ్చు. కాబట్టి ప్రశ్న “ఆఫీస్ మంచిదా, ఇంటినుంచి పని మంచిదా” అనేది మాత్రమే కాదు. ఏ పని కోసం ఏ విధానం సరిపోతుంది అన్నది సందర్భాన్ని బట్టి చూడాలి.
listeningScripts.romanization: intinunchi pani cheyadam valla prayana samayam taggutundi, kondariki ekaagrata koodaa peragochchu. ade samayamlo, team-lo anaupachaarikangaa jarige chinna sambhaashanalu taggipothe samaachaaram panchukovadam, kottavaallu team-lo kalavadam kaasta kashtamavachchu. kaabatti prashna office manchidaa, intinunchi pani manchidaa anedi maatrame kaadu. ae pani kosam ae vidhaanam saripotundi annadi sandarbhaanni batti choodaali.

summary.en: The speaker reframes remote work as a context-dependent trade-off.

listeningScripts.title: Literal and implied meaning
listeningScripts.transcriptTelugu: ఒక సంభాషణను అర్థం చేసుకోవడానికి మాటల అక్షరార్థం మాత్రమే చాలదు. ఎవరు ఎవరితో మాట్లాడుతున్నారు, వాళ్ల మధ్య సంబంధం ఏమిటి, ముందు ఏం జరిగింది, ఏ మాటను ఏ ధోరణిలో చెప్పారు అన్నవి కూడా అర్థాన్ని మార్చగలవు. ఉదాహరణకు, “చూద్దాం” అనే మాట నిజంగానే తర్వాత పరిశీలిద్దాం అనే అర్థంలో ఉండొచ్చు; కొన్నిసార్లు నేరుగా “లేదు” అనకుండా సంభాషణను ముగించడానికి కూడా వాడవచ్చు. అందుకే అధిక స్థాయి భాషా నైపుణ్యం అంటే సందర్భం ఆధారంగా ఉద్దేశాన్ని అంచనా వేసి, అవసరమైతే ఆ అంచనాను సరిచేసుకోవడం కూడా.
listeningScripts.romanization: oka sambhaashananu artham chesukovadaaniki maatala aksharaartham maatrame chaaladu. evaru evarito maatlaadutunnaaru, vaalla madhya sambandham emiti, mundu em jarigindi, ae maatanu ae dhoranilo cheppaaru annavi koodaa arthaanni maarchagalavu. udaaharanaku, chooddaam ane maata nijangaane tarvaata parisheeliddaam ane arthamlo undochchu; konnisaarlu nerugaa ledu anakundaa sambhaashananu muginchadaaniki koodaa vaadavachchu. anduke adhika sthaayi bhaashaa naipunyam ante sandarbham aadhaarangaa uddeshaanni anchanaa vesi, avasaramaithe aa anchanaanu sarichesukovadam koodaa.

summary.en: Advanced comprehension requires interpreting intention from context, not only literal words.

comprehensionQuestions.en: What two readings of “చూద్దాం” are offered?

listeningScripts.title: Context listening 1
listeningScripts.transcriptTelugu: ఈరోజు పని కొంచెం ఎక్కువగా ఉంది. మధ్యాహ్నం ఒక మీటింగ్ ఉంది. సాయంత్రం ఫ్రెండ్‌ని కలవాలి.
listeningScripts.romanization: ee roju pani konchem ekkuvagaa undi. madhyaahnam oka meeting undi. saayantram friend-ni kalavaali.

summary.en: Work is a little heavy today. There is a meeting in the afternoon. I need to meet a friend in the evening.

comprehensionQuestions.en: What plan, problem or reason is mentioned?

listeningScripts.title: Context listening 2
listeningScripts.transcriptTelugu: మధ్యాహ్నం ఒక మీటింగ్ ఉంది. సాయంత్రం ఫ్రెండ్‌ని కలవాలి. రేపు ఉదయం త్వరగా బయల్దేరాలి. ట్రాఫిక్ ఎక్కువగా ఉండొచ్చు.
listeningScripts.romanization: madhyaahnam oka meeting undi. saayantram friend-ni kalavaali. repu udayam tvaragaa bayalderaali. traffic ekkuvagaa undochchu.

summary.en: There is a meeting in the afternoon. I need to meet a friend in the evening. I need to leave early tomorrow morning. Traffic may be heavy.

regionalComprehension.policy: Teach a broadly understandable contemporary Telugu for production. Train comprehension of Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema and Telangana variation without ranking varieties as correct/incorrect or forcing imitation.
taskTypes: infer unfamiliar surface form from context
identify shared meaning despite pronunciation/lexical variation

cultureAndInteraction.rule: Respectful plural/polite forms and kinship/address terms depend on age, familiarity, relationship and setting; teach choices contextually, not as rigid rules.
Do not assume one universal naming/address convention; model polite alternatives and let context guide usage.
Teach practical language without presenting one regional food practice as universal Telugu culture.
Indirectness varies by relationship and situation. Do not encode one phrase as always meaning refusal/acceptance.
Learners should recognise when casual, polite, professional and formal language choices change interpersonal meaning.
Treat variation descriptively and respectfully; comprehension flexibility is the goal.

learnerErrorCorpus.errorOrRisk: Using “మీరు ఏమిటి?” for “What is your name?”
learnerErrorCorpus.preferredCorrection: Use “మీ పేరు ఏంటి?” for the natural name question.
learnerErrorCorpus.teachingNote: Avoid literal word-for-word translation from English.

learnerErrorCorpus.errorOrRisk: Using a new word in a test before meaning is shown
learnerErrorCorpus.preferredCorrection: Preteach meaning, spoken form, script, romanization and context first.
learnerErrorCorpus.teachingNote: This is a product/content error, not a learner error.

learnerErrorCorpus.errorOrRisk: Mixing casual “నువ్వు” with polite verb/address forms without context
learnerErrorCorpus.preferredCorrection: Keep pronoun/register choices consistent with relationship unless explicitly teaching a shift.
“మనం” includes the listener; “మేము” excludes the listener.

learnerErrorCorpus.errorOrRisk: Translating “I like X” as English subject-verb order
learnerErrorCorpus.teachingNote: Telugu commonly uses dative experiencer for liking.

learnerErrorCorpus.preferredCorrection: Learn place forms in chunks: Xకి వెళ్లాలి vs Xలో ఉన్నాను.

learnerErrorCorpus.errorOrRisk: Overusing bookish equivalents in casual speaking
learnerErrorCorpus.preferredCorrection: Prefer common spoken forms when appropriate; teach formal equivalents as register variants.

learnerErrorCorpus.errorOrRisk: Using one memorised sentence as the only accepted response

learnerErrorCorpus.preferredCorrection: Use connectors and discourse markers to build a coherent explanation.

learnerErrorCorpus.errorOrRisk: Sounding overly certain when evidence is weak

learnerErrorCorpus.preferredCorrection: Interpret with context/tone; it can be literal or indirect.
Switch register according to relationship and setting.
Fluency includes coherent, well-paced spontaneous expression and repair, not raw speed.
Qualify scope and distinguish evidence from inference.

learnerErrorCorpus.errorOrRisk: Forcing one interpretation of ambiguous language
learnerErrorCorpus.preferredCorrection: Preserve ambiguity and present plausible alternatives when evidence is insufficient.

Summarise two viewpoints on the same familiar issue and state where they agree/disagree.

readingCorpus.telugu: సౌకర్యం పెరిగినప్పుడు మనం ఏ సమాచారం పంచుకుంటున్నాం, దానికి బదులుగా ఏ ప్రయోజనం పొందుతున్నాం అన్నది కూడా చూడాలి. ప్రతి సందర్భంలో ఒకే నిర్ణయం సరిపోదు.

readingCorpus.telugu: ఒక నిర్ణయాన్ని కేవలం ఫలితంతోనే అంచనా వేయడం సరిపోదు. ఆ నిర్ణయం తీసుకున్న సమయంలో అందుబాటులో ఉన్న సమాచారం ఏమిటి, ప్రత్యామ్నాయాలు ఏమిటి, ప్రమాదాలు ఎలా అంచనా వేశారు అన్నది కూడా చూడాలి.

meaning.en: A decision should not be judged only by its outcome; available information, alternatives and risk assessment at the time also matter.

readingCorpus.telugu: భాషలో అస్పష్టత ఎప్పుడూ లోపం కాదు. కొన్నిసార్లు సంబంధాన్ని కాపాడటానికి, నిర్ణయాన్ని తెరిచి ఉంచటానికి లేదా మాటను ఉద్దేశపూర్వకంగా మృదువుగా చేయటానికి మాట్లాడేవారు ప్రత్యక్షంగా చెప్పకుండా ఉండవచ్చు. అయితే అదే అస్పష్టత బాధ్యతను తప్పించుకోవడానికి కూడా ఉపయోగపడవచ్చు; తేడాను సందర్భమే చూపుతుంది.

meaning.en: Ambiguity is not always a flaw; it can preserve relationships or soften communication, but it can also avoid responsibility, and context determines the difference.

writingSecondaryTrack.principle: Writing does not gate early spoken progression. At higher levels, short-to-long writing tasks can provide additional evidence of grammar/register but speaking/listening remain primary.

principles: Use actual native-speaker pacing, not simply sped-up learner audio.
Include fillers, repairs, repetitions, discourse markers, natural pauses and connected speech.
Progress from gist to detail to inference to shadowing/response.
Allow replay in learning mode; reduce replay support in assessments.
At C1-C2 include multiple speakers, digressions, informal speech, telephone/noisy conditions and unfamiliar accents after acclimatisation.

stages.A0-A1: clear natural speech with controlled vocabulary and optional slower replay
stages.A2: normal short everyday speech with repair support
stages.B2: native-speed everyday and professional speech with colloquial markers
stages.C1: long unscripted speech, unfamiliar accents after acclimatisation, idiomatic language
stages.C2: extended natural-speed interaction with implicit meaning, variation, competing viewpoints and imperfect audio conditions

engineBinding.conceptIdentity: Stable concept IDs never depend on mutable Telugu spelling or English base-language text.
engineBinding.firstExposureRule: Before a lexical concept can be graded, show English meaning, spoken Telugu, Telugu script, romanization, audio and at least one natural context.
engineBinding.hoverGlossRule: Every learner-facing word/chunk resolves to an English gloss in learning mode; future base languages add parallel gloss values.
engineBinding.dependencyRule: A0-A2 cannot require unexplained lexical concepts. B1-C2 may use deliberate unknowns only in explicit inference tasks with post-attempt gloss access.
engineBinding.multiHourRule: Each session can introduce additional new concepts if recall/retention remains healthy; studying 3-4 hours must not trap the learner in the same first 60 words.
engineBinding.failedRecallRule: Re-teach/review earlier in a different context; do not simply repeat the identical card indefinitely.
engineBinding.progressionRule: Lesson completion never equals mastery. Advance from evidence accumulated across time and contexts.
engineBinding.c2Rule: C2 cannot unlock from item completion alone; require repeated unseen C2-level performance.

practiceGenerationContract.purpose: Generate large exercise variety only from approved language atoms/patterns without inventing unreviewed Telugu at runtime.
rules: Use only approved patterns and morphologically approved slot forms.
Never concatenate case suffixes blindly; store valid surface forms.
Never introduce an unexplained concept in required beginner output.
Generated drills are practice instances, not new linguistic facts.
Prefer native-reviewed fixed examples over generated examples.
Speaking answers may have multiple accepted semantic/pragmatic variants.

hoverGlossContract.rule: Every learner-facing Telugu word/chunk must resolve to a concept or contextual gloss in learning mode.
hoverGlossContract.futureBaseLanguageSupport: Add meaning.<languageCode> without changing Telugu IDs.
hoverGlossContract.advancedInferenceException: B1-C2 inference tasks may temporarily hide a gloss until after the learner attempts inference; the gloss remains available afterward.

C1: use language flexibly for social/professional purposes
C2: understand virtually all normal spoken language after reasonable acclimatisation
perform spontaneously on unseen demanding tasks

reviewStatusDefinitions.model_reviewed: internally checked for structure/meaning/naturalness but not a substitute for native linguistic certification
reviewStatusDefinitions.generated_needs_native_review: validity/naturalness should be checked by a native reviewer before production release
reviewStatusDefinitions.native_review_required: especially sensitive to register, dialect, idiom, phonetics or pragmatics; must be native-reviewed before production release
reviewStatusDefinitions.native_approved: may only be set by an actual authorised human/native review workflow

releaseChecklist: All production-target Telugu reviewed for meaning/naturalness/register.
Audio recorded or approved by native Telugu speakers/TTS QA.
Every A0-A2 required token dependency resolvable before exercise.
No bookish-only form used as default everyday production target when a common spoken form is intended.
Romanization checked against audio, not merely spelling.
Regional exposure reviewed by speakers familiar with the represented variety.
All external corpus material, if later imported, has provenance/license metadata.
C2 certification uses unseen tasks, not memorised item completion.
